title: pharmacy acquisition credit committee memo
instruction:
You’re Genevieve Eberhardt, the pharmacist leading acquisition compliance review for Flintridge Clinic, and Kwame Boateng needs your judgment before he takes the proposed purchase of the Pinehollow Regional Office pharmacy operation to credit committee on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. Flintridge proposes to acquire the seller’s prescription files, saleable inventory, fixtures, and leasehold position at an October 18 closing for $2.85 million, funded with a requested $2.25 million seven-year term loan and $600,000 of buyer equity. The preliminary credit summary labels pharmacy risk “acceptable” because the seller reported $620,000 of adjusted EBITDA and the site remains profitable, but that label was entered before pharmacy review. You are authorized to replace it with your assessment and recommendation. Fiona Okonkwo, who chairs committee, wants a single page that Kwame can carry into the meeting and defend without opening the 140-page data room or three years of claims extracts. Two committee members understand pharmacy reimbursement and ownership transitions; the others do not, so the memo has to make the consequences intelligible without becoming a pharmacy tutorial. Assess the transaction under Pennsylvania pharmacy requirements as of August 15, 2026 and make exactly one recommendation on the loan request. Either a tightly conditioned approval or a deferral on the current record can be defensible, but an unqualified approval is not. End with the decision itself, not a list of next steps. Anchor the recommendation in one decision-useful number and keep that number consistent wherever it appears. The current review record is as follows. Prescription volume was 78,400 in FY2024, 72,900 in FY2025, and 64,800 in the FY2026 annualized claims run; revenue for those periods was $12.4 million, $11.7 million, and $10.6 million. The seller attributes the decline to temporary technician vacancies, but the claim-level attribution accounts for the 13,600-script reduction from FY2024 to FY2026 as 9,700 prescriptions lost after the site’s largest referring prescriber group relocated, 2,100 lost after a payer network exclusion, and 1,800 from general attrition. There is no executed referral replacement or documented volume-recovery plan. Payer A represents 47% of current scripts and 52% of gross reimbursement; Payers B and C represent another 19% and 13% of scripts and 16% and 11% of gross reimbursement, respectively. Gross reimbursement per script fell from $124.60 in FY2024 to $116.20 in FY2026, while the amount remaining per script after ingredient cost, dispensing-related fees, and known retrospective concessions fell from $12.40 to $8.10. Payer A has notified the seller of a November 1, 2026 reset expected to reduce that remaining amount by another $2.80 on its scripts if the current mix holds. A separate year-end reconciliation exposure is estimated at $180,000 to $310,000. People in committee routinely use “effective reimbursement rate” in two different ways: some mean gross reimbursement per prescription, while others mean the amount remaining after acquisition cost, fees, and concessions. If you use that term, make its meaning unambiguous before drawing a conclusion from it. The seller’s $620,000 adjusted EBITDA includes owner add-backs and assumptions that underwriting has not accepted. The current lender case is $355,000 before the Payer A reset and $270,000 after its estimated effect, against annual debt service of $318,000. Chidi Blackwood has also described $145,000 of purchasing and staffing synergies, but there are no executed vendor terms, staffing schedules, or other support for including that amount in debt-service capacity. Do not invent forecasts, valuations, rates, recovery percentages, or mitigants beyond arithmetic derived from these figures. The compliance review also found an open Pennsylvania State Board of Pharmacy consent order naming Helena Kilgore, the seller’s pharmacist-in-charge, effective February 12, 2025 through February 11, 2027. It arose from controlled-substance recordkeeping and inventory-reconciliation failures and requires quarterly controlled-substance audits, documented corrective action, and enhanced pharmacist supervision. The order does not name Flintridge Clinic or its proposed pharmacist-in-charge, but it will still be open at the proposed closing, and the operating plan currently assumes Helena will remain through transition. No one has documented how the order affects that reliance, whether its obligations attach to Helena, the existing permit, or both, or what the buyer must have in place before operating. The premises lease runs through September 30, 2030 at base rent of $18,500 per month. It prohibits assignment or subletting without the landlord’s prior written consent and gives the tenant no unilateral assignment right. The seller reports that the landlord is supportive, but there is no signed consent, amendment, or replacement lease. The pharmacy’s licensed location, prescription-file transition, payer participation, and opening plan all assume uninterrupted possession, while the requested loan would remain outstanding beyond the current lease term. No final ownership-change filing, buyer pharmacy permit, payer enrollment confirmation, controlled-substance inventory protocol, or patient communication plan is in the credit file. Keep patient and prescriber identities out of the memo and use only the minimum sensitive detail needed to explain the risks. Clearly distinguish established facts, seller or management representations, calculated implications, and matters that remain unresolved; do not imply that a consent order, pharmacy permit, DEA registration, payer contract, lease, or prescription relationship automatically transfers merely because assets are being purchased. Write the finished one-page lender acquisition memo as `pinehollow_acquisition_memo.pdf` at the top level of the working directory using exactly that filename. It must stand on its own for the mixed-background committee, identify what changed from the preliminary pharmacy-risk label, give one clear credit recommendation supported by the economics and the material pharmacy, regulatory, payer, and lease issues, and fit on one readable page.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `pinehollow_acquisition_memo.pdf` — One-page pharmacist-prepared acquisition and compliance assessment for the lender’s credit committee. (Must be written to the top level of the working directory using exactly the required filename.; Must contain exactly one readable page.; Must make exactly one recommendation on the loan request and end on that decision.; Must assess Pennsylvania pharmacy requirements as of August 15, 2026.; Must not contain patient or prescriber identities.; Must not invent forecasts, valuations, rates, recovery percentages, or mitigants beyond arithmetic derived from the stated figures.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

spec.professional_context: A pharmacist is providing the final pharmacy-compliance and operating-risk assessment for a lender considering financing an asset acquisition. The memo must support a near-term credit decision while accurately translating pharmacy-specific exposure for a mixed-background committee.
difficulty_sources: A one-page limit forces disproportionate emphasis on four risks that would be buried by proportional summarization.
The reported profitability and preliminary acceptable-risk label conflict with normalized and stressed repayment capacity.
The audience mixes pharmacy-literate and non-pharmacy credit stakeholders.
A routinely used reimbursement term has two materially different meanings.
The open consent order creates a distinction between named-party liability and practical transition exposure.
The lease, licensing, payer, controlled-substance, privacy, and patient-transition issues interact at the proposed closing.
Two decision postures are defensible, but the practitioner must choose and support only one.

authoring_plan.solver_instance: A retail-pharmacy compliance pharmacist translating acquisition diligence into a one-page lender decision memo.
authoring_plan.intended_verdict: An unconditional approval is not supported. The gold may either defer the request on the current record or approve only subject to decision-critical pre-funding and pre-operation conditions. It must select one posture, not present both.

planted_tension.headline_case: Reported adjusted EBITDA appears adequate and created a preliminary acceptable-risk label.
planted_tension.controlling_evidence: Normalized earnings provide only thin pre-reset coverage, the supported stressed case falls below debt service, most script loss is structural, payer exposure is concentrated, the order remains open at closing, and occupancy is not assignable without written landlord action.
planted_tension.acceptable_resolution_A: Conditioned approval, with enforceable conditions addressing occupancy, pharmacy ownership authorization, pharmacist-in-charge readiness, controlled-substance authority and inventory, payer continuity, order implications, and repayment capacity.
planted_tension.acceptable_resolution_B: Deferral on the current record until those same matters are resolved and a supportable coverage case exists.

gold_relationships: Transaction sources equal the purchase price: requested debt plus buyer equity equals total consideration.
Total script decline equals FY2024 scripts minus FY2026 annualized scripts.
The three attributed causes sum exactly to the total script decline.
The relocation cause divided by total decline is approximately 71.3%, supporting a structural rather than temporary interpretation.
Top-three script concentration equals the sum of the three stated script shares.
Top-three gross-reimbursement concentration equals the sum of the three stated reimbursement shares.
Pre-reset DSCR equals lender-case cash flow divided by annual debt service.
Stressed DSCR equals post-reset lender-case cash flow divided by annual debt service and is below 1.00x.
The estimated annual Payer A reset effect may be derived by multiplying annualized scripts by Payer A’s script share and the per-script reduction.
The consent order remains active at the proposed closing because its end date follows closing.
The seven-year loan extends beyond the stated lease expiration.
The Payer A reset follows shortly after the proposed closing.
professional_rules_expected: Distinguish an asset acquisition from automatic transfer of permits, registrations, payer participation, prescription relationships, and lease rights.
Treat buyer pharmacy authorization and an eligible pharmacist-in-charge as operational prerequisites rather than post-closing cleanup.
Treat DEA authority as registrant- and location-specific and require lawful controlled-substance inventory and transfer documentation.
Separate the named pharmacist’s consent-order exposure from the buyer’s legal status while recognizing transition, supervision, and permit implications.
Treat written occupancy control as essential to operation of a location-licensed pharmacy.
Recognize payer enrollment and network continuity as transaction dependencies.
Protect patient choice, privacy, continuity, and record custody during prescription-file transfer.
Limit inventory value to stock that is lawfully transferable and saleable.
Exclude unsupported synergies and unsupported recovery assumptions from reliable debt-service capacity.
Use evidence labels that distinguish verified facts, representations, calculations, and unresolved matters.

terminology_control.required_handling: The gold must either define the term before use or avoid it in favor of consistently unambiguous labels.
distinct_measures: Amount remaining per prescription after ingredient cost, dispensing-related fees, and known retrospective concessions.

authoring_plan.audience_test: A lender without pharmacy background must understand the credit consequences, while a pharmacy-literate reviewer must still find the distinctions technically accurate. The memo should not become a tutorial.
authoring_plan.privacy_test: No patient or prescriber identity should appear. Sensitive regulatory detail should be limited to what is necessary to explain transaction and operating risk.
authoring_plan.completion_test: The final substantive line must be the selected loan decision. The same numerical decision anchor must agree everywhere it appears, and all four material issues must visibly influence the recommendation.

deliverables.description: One-page pharmacist-prepared acquisition and compliance assessment for the lender’s credit committee.
constraints: Must be written to the top level of the working directory using exactly the required filename.
Must contain exactly one readable page.
Must make exactly one recommendation on the loan request and end on that decision.
Must assess Pennsylvania pharmacy requirements as of August 15, 2026.
Must not contain patient or prescriber identities.
Must not invent forecasts, valuations, rates, recovery percentages, or mitigants beyond arithmetic derived from the stated figures.
